subject: Acme pricing estimate & next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Liza Chen <liza@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Discovery + pricing parameters (token volumes / target $/1M)

Hi Liza —

Thanks for the 30-min call today — helpful to get a sense of Acme's usage patterns and priorities. Quick recap and the asks I said we'd follow up on: 

Summary from call:
- Workloads: product search & summarization for customer support (short chat turns) + weekly batch embedding jobs for analytics.
- Expected steady-state token volume: ~50M input+output tokens/day (spikes up to ~80M/day during promotions).
- Growth: 20–30% q/q over next 6 months.
- Primary SLO: 95p latency under 600ms for interactive calls.
- Constraints: budget target of roughly $12k–$18k / month to start; target unit goal ~ $10–$18 per 1M tokens depending on model mix.

Next items I'm sending:
1) A pragmatic invoice estimate + cost model that maps your projected token volumes to per-M token economics and recommended model/quantization mixes. (See attached: ACME_invoice_estimate_20260715.xlsx and acme_pricing_breakdown_20260715.pdf)
2) A short list of questions where we need clarification to tighten the cost model (see inline below).

Clarifying Qs (please reply inline or in Slack):
- For interactive chat: what percent of calls do you expect to be single-turn vs multi-turn? (multi-turn increases context window usage and KV cache costs)
- For embeddings: how many vectors per user / batch frequency? (affects indexing vs inference cost)
- Do you have any contractual constraints (e.g., strict data residency or E2E encryption requirements) beyond what's in your RFP?

Proposed next steps:
- You review the attached estimate and let me know which assumptions you'd like adjusted (model choice, target latency, discount expectations).
- If it looks reasonable, we can prepare a formal invoice + contract and loop in procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop back on a quick call with Marissa (solutions) if you want us to walk through the spreadsheet line-by-line.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0184
Redwood Inference

From: Liza Chen <liza@acme.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:02:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Discovery + pricing parameters (token volumes / target $/1M)

Hi Sean —

Thanks for the recap and for sending the attachments. Quick answers to your questions below:

- Interactive chat mix: ~70% single-turn (short prompts/answers), ~30% multi-turn with average history of 3–4 turns.
- Embeddings: initial launch will index new content nightly; roughly 3M vectors/month to start, with each embedding call returning one vector per doc.
- No additional residency constraints beyond us being in the US (we do want SOC2 + standard audit logs).

Budget context: leadership gave us an initial budget band of $12k–$18k/mo for the first 3 months while we validate the feature. If the numbers require higher spend to hit SLOs, we can revisit.

Can you confirm the assumption you used for average tokens per interactive call in the spreadsheet? That will help us validate your per-1M token numbers. Also would appreciate a short note on how caching / batching might lower the effective unit cost.

Happy to sync after you've updated the estimator.

Thanks,
Liza
Director, ML Platforms
Acme Corp
From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
To: Liza Chen <liza@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Acme invoice estimate & cost model (follow-up)

Liza —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the extra detail — that's super helpful. I updated the attached estimator with your 70/30 single vs multi-turn split and the 3M vectors/mo embedding baseline. Key assumptions and highlights below: 

Assumptions used in estimator (tab: Summary):
- Interactive average tokens per call: 120 tokens (input+output). Multi-turn sessions modeled as 4 turns * 120 tokens = 480 tokens per session, but we apply KV-cache efficiency so incremental cost per extra turn is ~40% of a cold context.
- Embeddings: 1 vector/doc, 3M vectors/month => ~300k embedding calls/day average when normalized across month.
- Model mix recommendation: 70% mid-sized open model (quantized) for chat; 30% larger model (unquantized) for higher-quality summarization.
- Target unit economics to hit ~$12k/month: blended effective cost ~ $12–$15 per 1M tokens after caching & batching + a Redwood platform fee margin.

Cost breakdown (high level):
- Model inference cost (cloud GPU ops) — 55% of token cost
- Platform (orchestration, caching, KV storage) — 20%
- Margin, support, and fixed overhead — 25%

What the estimate contains (attachments):
- ACME_invoice_estimate_20260715.xlsx: line-item monthly cost for starting config, 3-month projection, and elasticity table for 25/50/100 M tokens/day.
- acme_pricing_breakdown_20260715.pdf: one-page executive view with per-1M token scenarios and recommended model mixes.

How caching & batching reduce cost:
- Prefix / KV caching avoids re-computing the encoder for repeated contexts and lowers per-turn compute by ~30–50% for multi-turn flows.
- Workload-aware batching (for embeddings and async jobs) reduces per-request overhead and can lower GPU utilization cost by ~20–40% depending on traffic shape.

Next steps:
1) If you confirm the token-per-call assumption (120 cold tokens), I'll update the estimator to show a sensitivity table with $/1M tokens at different cache hit rates.
2) If the ranges look good, we'll generate a formal invoice and a short-term commitment (monthly) to start; we can document an automatic rollback to on-demand after 90 days if volume doesn't match projections.

I've re-attached both files and uploaded them to a share link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2B3C4D5E6F/view?usp=sharing

Would you like Marissa and me to walk the spreadsheet over a 20-min call tomorrow?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0184
